detailed_rationale:
IndusInd Bank is a post-crisis recovery story, not yet a clean bank. [DATA] The FY25 blow-up had three distinct legs: (1) incorrect internal accounting of derivative trades used to hedge forex borrowings (early-termination mismatches booked as notional profit rather than mark-to-market), which the bank's own March-2025 disclosure sized at ~2.35% of net worth, and which Grant Thornton's forensic review later quantified as a cumulative adverse P&L impact of Rs 1,959.98 cr as of 31-Mar-2025; (2) a separate, whistleblower-triggered discovery in the microfinance (Bharat Financial Inclusion) business of Rs 674 cr wrongly booked as interest income across three quarters of FY25 (fully reversed by 10-Jan-2025) plus Rs 172.58 cr wrongly classified as fee income across FY24-25; and (3) Rs 595 cr of unsubstantiated 'other assets' balances, netted off against 'other liabilities' in January 2025, that the bank itself said were likely the result of fraudulent activity by employees. All three were absorbed into a single quarter: IndusInd reported a consolidated net LOSS of Rs 2,329 cr in Q4FY25, dragging full-year FY25 net profit down 71% YoY to Rs 2,576 cr (still positive only because the first three quarters were clean). This is the correct way to read the hit — one-time, fully booked, not smoothed across periods.

Leadership fallout was real and, in hindsight, foreshadowed: MD&CEO Sumant Kathpalia resigned in April 2025 taking moral responsibility, and Deputy CEO/ED Arun Khurana resigned alongside him — notably, RBI had granted Kathpalia only a 1-year reappointment extension (not the 3 years the board sought) in the cycle before the scandal broke, a governance tell the market under-weighted at the time. The bank ran via a Committee of Executives during the interim before RBI approved Rajiv Anand (ex-Axis Bank Deputy MD, 35 years' banking experience) as the new MD&CEO; he took charge 25-Aug-2025 for a 3-year term to Aug-2028, and Arijit Basu was RBI-approved as Part-time Chairman on 19-Jan-2026 — so the leadership binary that dominated 2025 is now resolved and has ~11 months of runway under the new regime. [DATA] What remains genuinely OPEN: RBI ordered a comprehensive forensic investigation (via Grant Thornton) specifically to fix individual accountability among senior management and the statutory auditors, and NFRA separately sought the audit report to assess whether the auditors need action; this research pass found no confirmed public closure of that accountability process (no named sanctions, penalties, or a formal 'case closed' statement) as of 20-Jul-2026 — this is a live, un-quantifiable tail risk (auditor action, further RBI penalties, litigation) rather than a resolved item, and should be treated as such rather than assumed closed.

On current trajectory, the recovery is real but incomplete. [DATA] Q4FY26 (quarter ended 31-Mar-2026): consolidated PAT Rs 594 cr, up 364% QoQ from Rs 128 cr in Q3FY26 (and a clean turnaround from the Rs 2,329 cr Q4FY25 loss); GNPA 3.43%, NNPA 1.00%, PCR ~71%; CRAR (Basel III) a comfortable 17.48%; NII Rs 4,371 cr; pre-provision operating profit Rs 2,295 cr, +1% QoQ 'despite lower loan books' (i.e., the book is still de-growing, not yet back to growth). Full-year FY26 consolidated PAT was Rs 889 cr, down sharply from Rs 2,576 cr in FY25 — that comparison overstates the deterioration because FY25's number was itself already crisis-depressed, but it confirms FY26 was a low-ROE rebuild year (implied full-year ROE roughly 1-1.5% on an estimated ~Rs 65,000 cr net worth). The microfinance book, the other clear stress point, is genuinely healing: gross slippages fell to Rs 504 cr from Rs 1,022 cr QoQ, and 31-90 DPD fell to 0.9% from 2.4% QoQ — real, verifiable improvement rather than a one-quarter blip claim. The board recommended a final FY26 dividend of Rs 1.50/share (record date 26-Jun-2026), the clearest signal yet that the board itself views the crisis as behind the P&L even if not behind the regulatory-accountability process. Q1FY27 (quarter ended 30-Jun-2026) results are due via board meeting/earnings call on 22-Jul-2026 — two days after this note — so this call does not have the benefit of the freshest data point.

Valuation: CMP ~Rs 1,021-1,029 (20-Jul-2026, 52-week range Rs 710.60-1,038), market cap ~Rs 70,426 cr against an estimated net worth of ~Rs 65,000-65,300 cr (Rs 64,546 cr as of Mar-2025 plus FY26 retained profit net of dividend), implying trailing P/B of roughly 1.05-1.10x — computed directly from market-cap/net-worth because online P/B fields for this name are noisy (one data source shows an obviously erroneous 834x, another shows 1.23x; neither reconciles cleanly, so the mkt-cap/book-value arithmetic is the more trustworthy number here). A Gordon-growth back-solve (P/B=(ROE-g)/(COE-g)) at ~1.05-1.10x book, assuming a ~14% cost of equity (elevated versus a clean private bank, appropriately, given the fresh governance scars) and a modest ~10% sustainable growth rate, implies the market is pricing a recovery to roughly 14% normalized ROE — i.e., close to IndusInd's own pre-crisis (~15%) ROE run-rate. That is a fairly full recovery assumption for a bank that has not yet delivered even one quarter of double-digit ROE post-crisis and whose loan book was still shrinking as of Q4FY26. In other words, the stock is not cheap on a forward-normalized basis — it is priced for a clean recovery story, not for a discount to compensate for the still-open accountability process or the not-yet-demonstrated return to growth.
recommendation_rationale: Hold, not Sell: the full quantum of the FY25 accounting/derivative/MFI lapses is now known, fully booked (one-time Rs 2,329 cr Q4FY25 loss), and not recurring; the leadership vacuum is closed (Rajiv Anand as MD&CEO since Aug-2025, new Part-time Chairman since Jan-2026); capital is ample (CRAR 17.48%); and the two hardest-to-fake asset-quality signals (MFI slippages, 31-90 DPD) are both improving sharply QoQ. That combination does not support a Sell call on forensic grounds — there is no hidden or growing stress visible in this data. Equally, this is not a name to rate favorably beyond Hold under V1's Sell/Hold framework: ROE is still severely depressed (~1-1.5% FY26), the loan book was still contracting as of Q4FY26, and — most importantly — the RBI-ordered forensic accountability process (auditor conduct, individual sanctions) has no confirmed public closure as of this research date, leaving a real, unquantifiable governance tail risk open. At ~1.05-1.10x book the market is already pricing close to a full recovery to pre-crisis ROE, so there is limited valuation cushion if Q1FY27 (due 22-Jul-2026, just after this note) or the accountability process disappoints. Net: real, verifiable progress, but not yet a clean bank and not cheap enough to be a high-conviction Hold either — a textbook 'hold and watch the next two data points' call.
summary: IndusInd Bank is recovering from a self-inflicted 2025 crisis — incorrect derivative accounting plus separate microfinance-book irregularities that forced a Rs 2,329 crore loss in one quarter and cost the CEO and deputy CEO their jobs. A year on, the numbers are healing: the bank returned to profit, capital is comfortable, a new CEO (ex-Axis Bank) has been in the seat for almost a year, and the microfinance stress that was the other big worry is visibly improving quarter on quarter. What is not yet closed is the regulator-ordered probe into who is individually accountable for the lapses, and profitability (return on equity) is still far below what this bank used to generate. The stock, at roughly book value, is already priced for a fairly complete recovery rather than for a discount — so we see it as a hold, not a name to exit, but also not one to add to without seeing the still-pending accountability outcome and the next quarter's numbers (due within days) confirm the recovery is durable.
positive_para: The crisis quantum is fully known and booked, not still trickling out: all three lapses (derivative mis-accounting ~Rs 1,960 cr per Grant Thornton, Rs 674 cr MFI interest misbooking, Rs 595 cr unsubstantiated other-assets balances) were absorbed in the single Q4FY25 loss quarter, and no new discrepancies of similar scale have surfaced since. Leadership is stabilized: Rajiv Anand, a 35-year banker from Axis Bank, has been MD&CEO since 25-Aug-2025 with a clean 3-year RBI-approved mandate to 2028, and a new Part-time Chairman was RBI-approved in Jan-2026 — the succession vacuum that defined 2025 is closed. Capital is ample at 17.48% CRAR, the microfinance book (the other major stress point) shows genuine quarter-on-quarter healing (slippages down to Rs 504 cr from Rs 1,022 cr, 31-90 DPD down to 0.9% from 2.4%), and the board's decision to recommend a Rs 1.50/share final dividend for FY26 signals the board itself sees the P&L crisis as behind it.
negative_para: Profitability has not recovered: FY26 consolidated PAT of Rs 889 cr on an estimated ~Rs 65,000 cr net worth implies an ROE in the low single digits, versus a pre-crisis run-rate closer to 15% — this is still a bank rebuilding trust and margin, not one back to form. The loan book was still contracting as of Q4FY26 ('despite lower loan books'), meaning the franchise-rebuild (deposit confidence, MFI/vehicle-finance growth) is incomplete. Most importantly, the RBI-ordered forensic investigation into individual accountability (senior management, statutory auditors) and NFRA's separate examination of the auditor's conduct have no confirmed public closure as of this research date — this is a live, unquantifiable governance and regulatory tail risk, not a resolved item, and it sits alongside a valuation (~1.05-1.10x book) that already prices in most of the recovery, leaving limited cushion if either the pending Q1FY27 print (due 22-Jul-2026) or the accountability process disappoints.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At CMP ~Rs 1,021-1,029 against an estimated net worth of ~Rs 65,000-65,300 cr, trailing P/B works out to roughly 1.05-1.10x (computed directly from market-cap/book-value since online P/B fields for this name are inconsistent/noisy). Back-solving P/B=(ROE-g)/(COE-g) with a ~14% cost of equity (elevated for the residual governance risk) and a modest ~10% sustainable growth rate implies the market is pricing a recovery to roughly 14% normalized ROE — i.e., close to IndusInd's own pre-crisis (~15%) level. That is a fairly complete recovery assumption for a bank that has not yet posted even one quarter of double-digit ROE since the crisis and whose book was still shrinking last quarter — so the stock is not cheap on a forward-normalized basis; it is priced for the recovery story to keep working, which argues for Hold rather than a value case for accumulation, and for Hold rather than Sell given there is no fresh forensic deterioration visible in the data.
